title: Donna Vaughan, 1010 Wins Anchor, Goes On 'Jeopardy!' - NewsBreak
text:
By Joe Wilkinson ,
9 hours ago Donna Vaughan Photo Credit: Sony Pictures TV Vaughan’s episode is scheduled to air Thursday, March 26. She will compete against a Brooklyn man, Jeff Bienstock, and dominant New Jersey resident Jamie Ding , a nine-day champion.
"I was pretty nervous,” Vaughan told Newsday . “People say to me, well you’re on the radio every day, so to you this is probably no big deal. I don’t really agree with that. On the radio you don’t have to worry about what you look like.”
Long Islanders have heard Vaughan’s voice on the radio for more than 30 years, first with WALK 97.5 and later at 1010 WINS, where she’s been a news anchor for more than 10 years. The station even recently promoted her interview with Gov. Kathy Hochul in preparation for a snowstorm in January.
Vaughan’s journey to the Alex Trebek Stage began in 2020, when her husband encouraged her to take the online test, Newsday reported. After completing that, passing two more audition rounds, and waiting months, she got the call to fly to Los Angeles and compete.
“You get about a month's notice to be on the show,” Vaughan told Newsday, adding she was informed in January. “And I thought in one month I am not going to add enough to my breadth of knowledge [by studying] to make a difference.”
When not working on the radio, Vaughan teaches as an adjunct professor at Suffolk County Community College. She will face a tough challenge on “Jeopardy!”, as defending champion Ding won his ninth straight game on Wednesday night despite missing the Final Jeopardy answer.
"I really just wanted to just go on, have a good time, not embarrass myself and make memories. I was not thinking I was going to be the next Tournament of Champions winner," Vaughan told Newsday. "And I think I accomplished my goals."
